Subject: Peregrine AI — Dedicated GPU portfolio recommendation and next steps

Samantha / Peregrine procurement team —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is a compact recommendation we discussed: a dedicated-capacity plan that balances unit cost, latency, and long-context memory needs across three GPU families (H100, A100, L4). The attachment (rdw-dedicated-portfolio-appendix.pdf) has the detailed sizing worksheets and MAU assumptions from your deck; I pulled the 6- and 12-month traffic profiles into peregrine_mau_estimates.xlsx.

Quick summary up front:
- Short/medium requests (<= 4k tokens): L4 gives best $/token for embeddings and high-QPS routes.
- Long-context / high-throughput golden paths (16k+ seqs or heavy beam work): H100 reduces end-to-end latency and avoids memory pinning for models with large KV caches.
- Mid-tier model serving and mixed workloads: A100 (80GB where needed) is the cost/throughput compromise for most OLTP inference.

Open questions we flagged on the call that would change mix materially: your 95th percentile token length per request, expected concurrency bursts (primary vs. global), and whether you require strict colocation for PHI-sensitive flows.

Requested next steps:
1) Dev and Marissa will propose a concrete fleet mix (percent by capacity) and fallback rules for the first 12 months.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive next week to validate perf targets and burst policy (I suggest Tue/Wed afternoon PT).
3) Procurement: once we lock the mix we'll push a draft committed-capacity term sheet with reserve and burst tiers.

I'm copying Dev/Marissa for technical sizing.

—David
David Kim
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

Thanks David — the summary is helpful. A couple of follow-ups before the deep dive:

1) On model mix: our main production workload is a hallucination-sensitive summarization model (~12–18k context typical) plus a lightweight embedding service for similarity that spikes with search.
2) For the summarization model: we plan to run a 70B decoder with a 40–50k KV cache when doing history-aware summarization — does that push us to 80GB+ class GPUs (H100 / A100-80)?
3) Burst behavior: we expect 3–4x bursts during peak business hours for the search layer and more modest 1.2–1.5x for summarization. If we commit to a base capacity, what does Redwood recommend for burst policy and buffer sizing?

Happy to confirm Tue afternoon for the technical session.

—Samantha

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Li <samantha@peregrine.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-03-26T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine AI — Dedicated GPU portfolio recommendation and next steps

Samantha — quick technical notes and a recommended starting fleet composition based on the details you shared. Quoting your note for context:

> "our main production workload is a hallucination-sensitive summarization model (~12–18k context typical) plus a lightweight embedding service for similarity that spikes with search."

Reality check and tradeoffs:
- Memory: Large decoder weights + large KV caches (40–50k entries) push you into >=40–80GB HBM per-device territory. A100-80GB and H100-80GB both handle large per-replica memory without aggressive model sharding or offloading. L4 (24GB) cannot host the full working set for that summarization model without multi-GPU sharding which increases latency and implementation complexity.
- Throughput & latency: H100 generally offers best single-replica throughput on mixed FP16/INT8 stacks and is more efficient for very long sequences because of better memory bandwidth and kernel optimizations. A100-80 is a close second and is a good balance when cost is a concern. L4 shines for short-context, high-QPS routes (embeddings, short chat, rerank).
- Cost: L4 has the lowest $/token for short requests; A100 sits in the middle; H100 is the most expensive per-hour but reduces engineering complexity and tail latency for the long-context golden path. For predictability we often recommend "memory-first" for the summarization model (A100-80 or H100) and a separate L4 pool for embeddings/search.

Concrete starter plan (12-month runway, assuming current MAU from your sheet):
- Dedicated base pool: 40% A100-80 (serve mid-tier models and most production traffic)
- Long-context pool: 30% H100 (pin for summarization and history-heavy sessions; used for 95th pct CT and heavy KV cache)
- Edge/high-QPS pool: 30% L4 (embeddings and short-chat paths; configured with aggressive batching and cache locality)

Why this mix?
- Keeps most traffic on A100 where price/perf is favorable for typical production loads.
- Isolates the most memory-sensitive paths on H100 to avoid cross-tenant memory pressure and to reduce tail latency.
- Uses cheap L4 capacity to soak the cost-sensitive, high-QPS embedding load.

Burst and fallback policy recommendation:
- Reserve base capacity for 70–80% of median load.
- Allow prioritized burst to a cross-region pool (hosted spare H100/A100) for 2–3x short windows; for search spikes we allow L4 autoscaling up to 4x with autoscaling cooldowns tuned to 30–60s.
- Fallback: if H100 capacity exhausted, fallback to A100 with an automatic model quantization/throughput profile that degrades precision but preserves latency SLA for urgent requests. For embedding spikes, failover to best-effort L4 with limited context where possible.

Operational notes:
- KV cache size and eviction policy: we recommend sticky cache shards on H100 and A100 pools; L4 can run a smaller ephemeral cache.
- Quantization: for summarization, test FP16 then TF32->INT8 (if model supports). For Peregrine's hallucination sensitivity, keep a conservative quantization policy on the H100 pool.
- Monitoring: enable token-level cost and 99/99.9th latency traces per route. We'll set up a per-route dashboard in Redwood Console before go-live.

Attachments: I attached a small worksheet that maps your MAU bands to expected GPU-hours and a simple cost sensitivity table.

—Dev

Samantha —

Thanks for the clarifying details. Based on Dev's sizing, our recommended commercial proposal (high-level):

Tiered reserved capacity proposal (draft):
- Base commit (12 months): 40% A100-80, 30% H100-80, 30% L4 — validated against your MAU file.
- Burst buffer: additional shared pool accessible as a paid burst tier (regional H100 + A100 spare nodes) sized to handle 3x peak for 6 rolling hours per day.
- Pricing: we will draft committed-rate discounts by tier (A100 base discount, H100 premium, L4 low-cost rate). Exact numbers in the term sheet once we finalize the fleet mix and SLA windows.

Deliverables for next week:
1) Technical deep-dive (Tue 2028-03-30 1:00pm PT) — Dev and Marissa to validate perf runs and KV cache sizing.
2) Redwood draft term sheet and SOW (we aim to deliver by Thu EOD) with the reserve/burst definitions and runbook for fallbacks.
3) Procurement checklist: we will include SOC 2 artifacts and required IP protections; procurement@redwood will follow up on signatures.

If that matches your expectations, Samantha, we'll lock the deep-dive slot and circulate the term sheet draft.

Best —
David
